source.cite: A. F. Tasch, H. Shin, C. Park, J. Alvis and S. Novak, J. Electrochem. Soc. 136(3), 810-814 (1989), doi 10.1149/1.2096748
source.conditions: B+ into bare n-type (100) silicon, 7 deg tilt, 30 deg rotation, room temperature; profiles measured by SIMS (68 implants); Pearson parameters fitted by the authors

model: N(x) = D1 f1(x) + D2 f2(x); f1, f2 Pearson densities normalised on [0, inf); D1 + D2 = DT (eq. 5, 6)

table_I.note: Table I, page 813, typed values. R and dRp in angstrom; S = skewness gamma, K = kurtosis beta

table_II_BF2.note: Table II, page 814 (BF2+, boron profile); used only to test the Pearson code on skewed and peaked shapes (BF2 is a molecule the description cannot hold)

fig5_D1_over_DT.note: Fig. 5, page 812, digitised by the lead on 19 Nov 2026: page rendered at 450 dpi; axis frame found from the pixels (D1/DT 1.0 at row 181, 0.8 at row 1093; 1e13 at column 276.5, 1e17 at 1470.5); marker centroids from dark-pixel blobs in a 23-pixel column window at each dose. Estimated reading uncertainty 0.002. At 1e16 the 25, 35 and 50 keV markers merge into one blob spanning 0.983 to 0.992; the three values are read from the blob's extent (uncertainty 0.003).
fig5_D1_over_DT.assignment: curves assigned by order: the paper states the main peak is more dominant at higher energy at low dose; 15 keV open squares (lowest), 25 keV diamonds, 35 keV filled squares, 50 keV diamonds (highest), 80 keV open circles (two points)
